influences.name: Andy Warhol
influences.context: Growing up, I saw artists and musicians I admired doing all sorts of things. Andy Warhol made movies and a magazine.

influences.name: Jean Cocteau
influences.context: Growing up, I saw artists and musicians I admired doing all sorts of things... Jean Cocteau, John and Yoko, my friend Terry Allen and David Lee Roth became an emergency medical technician—for all of them exploring, and sometimes failing, was celebrated.

influences.context: with Brian's encouragement we discovered that we could improvise stuff in the studio, make a structure out of that

influences.name: Tosca String Quartet
influences.context: Having worked with those guys I decided, 'I will do a record with that kind of sound.'

influences.name: Stephen Barber
influences.context: Stephen Barber did most if not all of the string arranging stuff... Even Stephen can do some pretty unusual stuff, but it's always in service of the song.

influences.name: Mauro Refosco
influences.context: Mauro [Refosco] is an incredibly tasteful percussion player... given the people involved — they are all respectful of what's important in a song

influences.name: Andre Malraux
influences.context: In his book The Voices Of Silence, Andre Malraux points out that paintings became the dominant art form for many centuries because you could carry them around.

influences.name: John Philip Sousa
influences.context: The John Phillips Sousa quotes in his essay "The Menace of Mechanical Music." As a bandleader you can imagine how he felt about encroaching recording technology—that recorded music is "like eating canned salmon by a trout stream."
